option_relations.rationale: Papillary hemangioma matches the dermoscopic and histopathological findings of the case, including irregular red lacunae, absence of septa, and ectatic thin-walled vessels with intravascular branching papillary structures.
Pyogenic granuloma does not match the specific histopathological features described in the case, such as intravascular branching papillary structures and hyaline globules in endothelial cells.
Hobnail hemangioma is a distinct entity with characteristic hobnail-shaped endothelial cells, which are not described in the case.
Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma is a specific type of hemangioma with a distinct clinical and histological appearance, which does not match the case description.
